headline: Woman's dismembered body parts found in Adabor canal
summary: Police recovered the head and hand of an unidentified woman from a canal in the capital's Adabor area on Saturday afternoon.
details: Police recovered the dismembered body parts of an unidentified woman from a canal in the Adabor area of Dhaka.
The recovery took place on Saturday afternoon from the 10 No. Hakkarpar canal.
Among the recovered parts, the woman's head and hand were found inside sacks.
Police stated that the identity of the woman has not yet been established.
Authorities are currently working to recover any remaining parts of the body from the canal.
The Criminal Investigation Department (CID) team has been informed and called in to assist in identifying the victim.

headline_marked: 3 men, including a former lawyer, [[found dead in separate Dhaka locations]]
headline: 3 men, including a former lawyer, found dead in separate Dhaka locations
summary: Police recovered the bodies of a 43-year-old former lawyer in Lalbagh and two unidentified men near the High Court Mazar and National Eidgah.
details: Police recovered the bodies of three men from separate locations in Dhaka today, including a former lower court lawyer named Anwar Hossain, 43.
Anwar's body was found in a rented room in Lalbagh around 11:30 am after a neighbor noticed a foul smell and discovered the body inside.
According to the Lalbagh Police Station OC, Anwar lived alone since September 1 and was reportedly depressed and addicted to drugs.
Police primarily suspect that Anwar died two or three days ago due to illness, though the matter is still under investigation.
Separately, the bodies of two unidentified men, aged approximately 45 and 65, were found on footpaths near the National Eidgah Maidan and the High Court Mazar.
Passersby informed the police after seeing the men lying on the footpaths; they were declared dead upon arrival at the DMCH emergency department.
All three bodies have been sent to the Dhaka Medical College morgue for autopsies to determine the exact cause of death.
A CID forensic team has been informed to help identify the two unidentified deceased men.
caption:

According to the Lalbagh Police Station OC, Anwar lived alone since September 1 and was reportedly depressed and addicted to drugs.

Police primarily suspect that Anwar died two or three days ago due to illness, though the matter is still under investigation.

Separately, the bodies of two unidentified men, aged approximately 45 and 65, were found on footpaths near the National Eidgah Maidan and the High Court Mazar.

Passersby informed the police after seeing the men lying on the footpaths; they were declared dead upon arrival at the DMCH emergency department.

All three bodies have been sent to the Dhaka Medical College morgue for autopsies to determine the exact cause of death.

A CID forensic team has been informed to help identify the two unidentified deceased men.
